doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: A new band with Stinson, Szabo and Bohanon, creating moods
summary: After the quintet he changed completely, starting from scratch with Albert Stinson, Gabor Szabo and George Bohannon and creating moods rather than tunes, ahead of Miles's stop-and-start approach.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Now you went through other personnel changes too.
Did this help to reinvigorate the sound or did you feel that after a certain point -­
Well when I broke that sound up, I changed completely. That’s when Albert Stinson, Gabor, and myself and George Bohannon, you know, got the (unintelligible) band, which was -­
So how did you then conceive of your next band or was this also a happenstance, it just came together as well?

Well first of all, I changed up because I wanted to change. I didn’t play any of the old music. We started from scratch, you know, getting ideas from each other and things like that and creating moods. As a matter of fact, we actually -- we didn’t create any music, we just created moods. I was doing stuff, you know, stop and start stuff really before Miles and them were doing that kind of stuff. We were playing opposite in San Francisco, he was at one club and I was at the other, which was two doors apart.
